name: CESR Journey
purpose: A complete working file for a CESR / Portfolio Pathway application in ICM
description: Start here, My plan, one page per HiLLO with Key Capability checklists and supervisor comments, supervision meeting hub, placement guidance, reflections, an evidence index and curated resources. Curriculum wording is left as placeholders to paste from the FICM source. Pair it with the Supervision meeting, Reflection, Evidence cover sheet and PDP page templates.
audience: ICM CESR / Portfolio Pathway candidates and their supervisors

content.text: read this page once, then work mostly in My plan and the HiLLO pages. Share this workspace with your supervisor (Settings → Invite, role Editor) so meetings and comments happen in the same place.
Describe cases in general terms, use relative dates, and anonymise every document before it goes anywhere near this workspace.

A working file for your CESR / Portfolio Pathway application in Intensive Care Medicine: one page per High-Level Learning Outcome, a place to plan, a running evidence index, and supervision meetings recorded where the evidence lives.
It is not a clinical record and not your formal portfolio submission — it is where you build the case, so that the submission is a matter of assembling what is already organised.
— one page per outcome: what is asked, what good evidence looks like, a Key Capability checklist, your evidence, supervisor comments, gaps.
— one page per meeting, started from the meeting templates in the gallery.
— unit-specific guidance seeded from existing documents.
— quick capture with the reflection template.
— every item of evidence in one table.
— GMC and FICM guidance, FAQs, what assessors look for.
What to share with your supervisor
Invite your supervisor as an Editor so they can write in the Supervisor comments callouts and co-edit meeting pages live.
Keep drafts and personal notes as Private pages (page menu) — they stay yours even in a shared workspace.
Before each meeting, tick the KCs you believe you have evidenced and link the evidence; the meeting page then writes itself.
Weekly: add new evidence to the Evidence index and the relevant HiLLO page
Monthly: review gaps on each HiLLO page and update My plan
Each placement: initial, mid-placement and end-of-placement meetings
Three months before submission: pre-submission meeting and readiness checklist
set a target, map your placements to the HiLLOs they will evidence best, and keep the milestones ticking over. Revisit monthly.
Read the current FICM curriculum and the GMC Portfolio Pathway guidance (see Resources)
Complete a baseline self-assessment against all 14 HiLLOs
Agree the plan with your supervisor at the initial meeting
Evidence mapped to every HiLLO, with no red gaps
Structured reference and verification of evidence arranged
CV, application form and evidence bundle drafted
Pre-submission meeting and readiness checklist complete

props.title: Faculty of Intensive Care Medicine
props.description: Curriculum for Training in ICM and Portfolio Pathway (CESR) guidance

props.title: General Medical Council
props.description: Specialist registration via the Portfolio Pathway: application, evidence rules, verification

content.text: The GMC route to the specialist register for doctors who have not completed a UK-approved training programme in the specialty, assessed on evidence that the applicant's knowledge, skills and experience are equivalent to those of a CCT holder.
How much evidence does each HiLLO need?

Enough to show the capability across the breadth the curriculum describes, from more than one source, over time. Quality and mapping matter more than volume; a smaller, well-mapped, verified bundle beats a large unstructured one.
Does evidence from outside the UK count?
Yes, where it is verifiable and demonstrates the capability. Check the current GMC guidance for verification requirements and time limits before relying on older evidence.
— your evidence, verified by named people
— every item tied explicitly to outcomes and capabilities
— recent evidence, or a clear account of maintained skills
— the range of settings and patient groups the curriculum expects
— not just what you did, but what you learned and changed
— no patient-identifiable information anywhere in the bundle
Build the file as you go; the application is then a matter of assembly, not archaeology.

name: Supervision meeting — Initial
purpose: Objectives, baseline against the HiLLOs, and the plan for the placement
description: Structured note for a initial supervision meeting. Candidate and supervisor edit it together during the meeting; agreed actions are to-dos.

content.text: hold this in the first fortnight of a placement. Fill the baseline together; be candid about gaps — they are the plan.
«WPBA assessors, courses, exposure the candidate needs»

name: Supervision meeting — Mid-placement
purpose: Progress against objectives, evidence reviewed, concerns and course corrections
description: Structured note for a mid-placement supervision meeting. Candidate and supervisor edit it together during the meeting; agreed actions are to-dos.

content.text: review the evidence gathered so far against the initial objectives and adjust the plan for the second half.

name: Supervision meeting — End-of-placement
purpose: Summary of achievement and the supervisor's overall comment for the record
description: Structured note for a end-of-placement supervision meeting. Candidate and supervisor edit it together during the meeting; agreed actions are to-dos.

content.text: the record that travels with the candidate: what was evidenced here, the supervisor's overall view, and what the next placement must cover.
«Supervisor: overall assessment of this placement — signed and dated»

name: Supervision meeting — Pre-submission
purpose: Readiness checklist, outstanding gaps and sign-off before the application goes in
description: Structured note for a pre-submission supervision meeting. Candidate and supervisor edit it together during the meeting; agreed actions are to-dos.

content.text: run through every item; anything unticked is a reason to delay. Sign-off means both of you believe the bundle is complete, verified and anonymised.
Every HiLLO has mapped, verified evidence with no red gaps
Evidence index complete and matches the bundle
CV and application form complete and consistent with the evidence
Structured references and verifiers confirmed and contactable
Reflections cover the breadth of the curriculum
«Candidate and supervisor: names, date, and statement of readiness»

name: Reflection
purpose: A structured reflective entry mapped to a HiLLO and Key Capability
description: What happened, so what, now what — with learning and actions, and the outcome it evidences. Anonymised by design.

content.text: write it within a week of the event, anonymised, and link it from the HiLLO page it evidences.
Describe cases in general terms, use relative dates, and anonymise every document before it goes anywhere near this workspace.
«the situation, in general terms — no identifiers, relative dates»
«why it mattered; what you thought and felt; what went well and less well»
«what you would do differently; what you need to learn or practise»

name: Evidence cover sheet
purpose: Front page for one item of evidence: what it is, what it shows, who verified it
description: Attach or link the anonymised evidence, state the HiLLOs and Key Capabilities it demonstrates and why, and record verification.

content.text: one sheet per item; keep the title identical to the Evidence index row.
«what the evidence is and the context»
«the explicit link between the evidence and the outcome»
«attach the anonymised document here (upload) or add a bookmark»

name: Personal development plan
purpose: Goals, actions and evidence of achievement with target dates
description: A simple PDP table plus review notes, suitable for appraisal and supervision.

content.text: three to five goals at a time; review at each supervision meeting or appraisal.
